Incumbent [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] U.S. Senator [[Paul Coverdell]] won a second term in office,{{cite web |last=Clerk of the U.S. House of Representatives |author-link=Clerk of the United States House of Representatives |title=Statistics of the Congressional Election of November 3, 1998 |url=https://clerk.house.gov/member_info/electionInfo/1998election.pdf |publisher=[[U.S. Government Printing Office]] |page=12}} becoming the first of his party to ever win reelection to the U.S. Senate from Georgia. Coverdell would remain in the Senate until his death on July 18, 2000. == Democratic primary == === Candidates === * Jimmy Allen Boyd, businessman * [[Michael Coles (businessman)|Michael Coles]], co-founder of [[Great American Cookies]] and [[1996 United States House of Representatives elections in Georgia|1996 nominee]] for U.S. representative === Results === {{Election box begin no change | title = Democratic primary results }} {{Election box winning candidate with party link no change | candidate = Michael Coles | party = Democratic Party (United States) | votes = 312,765 | percentage = 76.14% }} {{Election box candidate with party link no change | candidate = Jimmy Allen Boyd | party = Democratic Party (United States) | votes = 98,020 | percentage = 23.86% }} {{Election box total no change | votes = 410,785 | percentage = 100.00% }} {{Election box end}} == General election == === Candidates === * [[Michael Coles (businessman)|Michael Coles]], co-founder of [[Great American Cookies]] and [[1996 United States House of Representatives elections in Georgia|1996 nominee]] for U.S. representative (Democratic) * [[Paul Coverdell]], incumbent U.S. senator since 1993 (Republican) * Daniel Fein (Socialist Workers) (''write-in'') * Bert Loftman (Libertarian) === Polling === {| class="wikitable" style="font-size:90%;text-align:center;" |- valign=bottom !
